Article Title: Ram Temple donation row: SC to hear plea against Champat Rai on Nov 2 over alleged irregularities
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has agreed to hear on November 2 a plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai

What is the case?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to hear on November 2 plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai and others over alleged irregularities in donations and land transactions linked to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to news agency ANI, the plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased in areas surrounding the temple.The plea also seeks the dissolution of the existing Trust and its complete reconstitution.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the petition would be taken up along with other pending pleas concerning the same.Earlier, Rai had been given a clean chit by the UP-State SIT, which probed the donation theft. He is listed in the chargesheet as a key prosecution witness. Chargesheet names as accused only eight arrested counting agents and employees for criminal breach of trust and corruption.Rai informed investigators that he first learned of the irregularities via a phone call and video message while travelling. He subsequently reviewed CCTV footage and suggested lodging the formal police complaint.The alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has triggered a political and administrative controversy. The issue came to light on June 7, when former Samajwadi Party MLA Pawan Pandey alleged that around Rs 7-7.5 crore from the daily offerings made by devotees had been siphoned off. He alleged that people associated with the temple’s management were involved in the alleged misappropriation.The allegations soon gained political traction after SP chief Akhilesh Yadav backed the claims and sought accountability. A section of local BJP leaders also called for an investigation, putting the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, which manages the temple, under increased scrutiny.The concerns grew after Nripendra Misra, chairman of the temple construction committee and a trust member, flagged loopholes in the existing system for handling and counting cash donations. He recommended appointing a professional CEO to strengthen oversight and transparency.Trust general secretary Champat Rai initially rejected the allegations. However, amid mounting scrutiny, the trust sought an investigation by the Uttar Pradesh government.The SIT submitted an interim report within a week, flagging procedural weaknesses in the system used to manage temple donations and recommending structural reforms to strengthen monitoring and accountability.The probe subsequently led to arrests in connection with the alleged irregularities.
Article Summary: Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeks legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai. The plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased in areas surrounding the temple.

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has questioned who authorised changes to the online Form 6 for voter registration and whether Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) was pressured to implement them.“The online Form 6 was changed illegally - as the EC's own Commissioners have recorded. Who at the ECI ordered Tata Consultancy Services to make that change? Who at TCS signed off on it? And were they pressured into doing it?” Rahul said in a post on X.The Election Commission has withdrawn the additional Special Intensive Revision (SIR)-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise has been completed, PTI reported on Wednesday.The declaration has been removed from the ECINET app and portal, as well as the respective Chief Electoral Officer portals, meaning new applicants in these states will only have to submit the regular statutory Form 6 for voter enrolment.In states and Union territories where the SIR exercise is still underway, the additional declaration remains available on the ECINET portal. Under the declaration, new applicants are required to provide details linking themselves, their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls prepared during an earlier SIR.The move follows a September 26 meeting of the full Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. After the meeting, the poll panel said the declaration attached to Form 6 was meant "specifically for SIR" and that “for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.”
Article Summary: The Election Commission has withdrawn the additional Special Intensive Revision (SIR)-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise has been completed. The move follows a September 26 meeting of the full Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

Article Title: Hate speech case: Mahua Moitra’s interim protection from arrest extended till January 2027
Article Text:
Mahua Moitra's interim protection from arrest extended

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Thursday extended till January 29, 2027, the interim protection granted to Mahua Moitra , MP from the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), in an alleged hate speech case.During the hearing, West Bengal advocate general Surojit Nath Mitra, appearing for the state government, submitted a report before the single-judge bench of Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya. The report noted that Moitra appeared before the Hogalberia police station in Nadia district on August 14 and answered the questions put to her by the investigating officer, in compliance with the court's earlier directions.The report further stated that the investigation into the alleged hate speech was still underway.Moitra's counsel told the court that the Krishnanagar MP was not subjected to egg pelting when she appeared at the police station on August 14. The lawyer had earlier alleged that Moitra faced such attacks whenever she visited her constituency in Nadia district.After hearing both sides, Justice Bhattacharyya extended Moitra's interim protection from coercive action in the case until January 29, 2027.The court fixed January 13 as the next date of hearing.In the petition, the TMC Mamata faction leader, has sought quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against her in connection with the case registered at Hogalberia police station on the complaint of a BJP worker. She has alleged that the case is based on “concocted and motivated allegations”.On July 21, Justice Bhattacharyya had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action in the case and directed her to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning.The court had ordered that no coercive action be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the conditions imposed by the court.Acting on a plea by her counsel, the judge had also directed the police to ensure that Moitra was not subjected to egg pelting when she appeared before the investigating officer.
Article Summary: Mahua Moitra, MP from the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), in an alleged hate speech case. She has sought quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against her in connection with the case registered at Hogalberia police station on the complaint of a BJP worker.

Article Title: ‘Might as well disband you’: SC slams UP police for cover-up job
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.

How will people trust police: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday slammed Uttar Pradesh police for not naming the accused in a road accident case despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police. It said it would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police worked with an agenda and did cover-up jobs.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.“In everything you have an agenda. How will people trust you if this is how you proceed with matters? It is better if we ask the CBI to step in all UP police investigations. We might as well disband UP police. This nonsense has to stop at some point,” the court said.Supreme Court added that the affidavit filed by Shobhit Kumar, circle officer of Khurja in Bulandshahr, who was directed to give an explanation, was “utterly uninspiring”.“Toeing the line is one thing but bending over is another. And this kind of cover up job... less said the better,” SC said and summoned the officer to be present in court to give an explanation on his conduct.“The said officer shall be present before court on next date to account for the same. It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why FIR No. 195/2026 was filed on Aug 19 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said rider was apprehended at the spot. In paragraph 6 of aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Prempal. The reason as to why the name was left blank in the FIR initially and was, thereafter, supplemented, requires to be explained,” the bench said in its order.The bench sought an explanation on why an FIR was filed against unknown person in the case. “Why did you write unknown if the person was caught at the spot? Why did you register the FIR against an unknown motorcycle rider if he was caught on the spot? How will people trust the police?” the bench asked.
Article Summary: Supreme Court slams Uttar Pradesh police for not naming the accused in a road accident case. It said it would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI. A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded.

Article Title: To Bengal plea on Congress pick, SC says will dismiss appeal
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Applying its recently framed policy of rejecting challenges to bails granted by high courts, Supreme Court on Wednesday told the West Bengal govt that it would dismiss the state's appeal against grant of interim bail to Milan Pradhan, Congress candidate for the Nandigram assembly bypoll, who is an accused in a 2007 murder case.A CJI-led bench expressed difficulty to list the matter on Thursday and said, "Instead of Thursday, we will dismiss the appeal on Monday."By Monday, electioneering for the bypoll would be over and the state's appeal would be infructuous. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state, requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for a hearing on Thursday of the appeal challenging the grant of interim bail to Pradhan for canvassing for the election scheduled for Oct 6, campaigning for which will end on Oct 4.When the bench said since the HC had granted only interim bail, it would not entertain such an appeal, Mehta brought up Pradhan's history sheet -- accused in a murder case and featuring in six other FIRs on serious crimes -- to request a hearing on Thursday.The HC had, citing the relief the SC gave to AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal, granted bail to Pradhan on Tuesday and asked him to surrender before the additional chief judicial magistrate, Haldia, on Oct 21.Counting of votes in Nandigram, which was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari who also won from Bhabanipur, will happen on Oct 9.The state said in its appeal, "The HC granted interim bail to Pradhan, an accused charged with multiple counts of heinous offences including murder, arson, bomb blasts and rioting with deadly weapons, solely on the untenable pretext of permitting him to participate in an election."It added, "The HC completely disregarded settled principles governing the grant of bail, overlooked the respondent's continuous evasion of judicial process for nearly two decades, ignored his active subversion of the criminal justice system, and exposed prosecution witnesses to imminent danger."
Article Summary: West Bengal govt appealed against grant of interim bail to Milan Pradhan, Congress candidate for the Nandigram assembly bypoll, who is an accused in 2007 murder case. A CJI-led bench expressed difficulty to list the matter on Thursday and said, 'Instead of Thursday, we will dismiss the appeal on Monday'

Article Title: Citing SC judge son, curative plea against verdict on CEC & ECs appointment law
Article Text:
The plea, filed by Jaya Thakur, said Justice Sharma's son Siddharth Sharma was standing counsel of the EC before Madhya Pradesh HC. It alleged that the judge's presence on the bench raised an apprehension of bias.

NEW DELHI: A curative plea has been filed in Supreme Court against a verdict on the law on appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and ECs, citing "reasonable apprehension of bias and propriety" on the part of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.DELHIThe plea, filed by Jaya Thakur, said Justice Sharma's son Siddharth Sharma was standing counsel of the EC before Madhya Pradesh HC. It alleged that the judge's presence on the bench raised an apprehension of bias.A two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sharma gave a split verdict on whether validity of the law should be referred to a constitution bench, but agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the issue.Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, has been challenged on the ground that the law gave the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee. The selection panel, comprising the PM, a cabinet minister and the LoP, gave the govt a 2:1 majority.While Justice Datta pointed out flaws in the law and said its validity could be examined by a division bench, Justice Sharma held that the issue had to be decided by a constitution bench.The petition said "a mere ground of appearance of bias and not actual bias is enough to vitiate the order" and argued that the judgment dated Sept 23 was vitiated due to Justice Sharma's presence.
Article Summary: A curative plea has been filed in Supreme Court against a verdict on the law on appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and ECs. The plea, filed by Jaya Thakur, said Justice Sharma's son Siddharth Sharma was standing counsel of the EC before Madhya Pradesh HC. It alleged that the judge's presence on the bench raised an apprehension of bias.

Article Title: Amid SIR row, INDIA bloc puts up united front, targets PM Modi, Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Upping the ante against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and PM Modi, the opposition INDIA bloc Wednesday announced a month-long nationwide agitation starting Oct 2, coinciding with the protest call given by various student bodies, including the Cockroach Janata Party, in Delhi and states. Crucially, the opposition collectively demanded that elections should revert to ballot papers from EVMs, and that pre-SIR electoral rolls be restored for future elections. It also sought an effective appeals mechanism for voters excluded from the rolls. The opposition has sought immediate resignation of the chief election commissioner.After deliberations, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge announced that the six-day agitation from Oct 2-8 would start with district-level "save democracy" protests. He said opposition MPs will march to the EC office in Delhi on Oct 6.Moving forward, the alliance will hold five major rallies in cities during Oct-Nov, including a mega rally in Delhi on Nov 1. The bloc appealed for expediting SC cases pertaining to SIR and electoral malpractices. To mount pressure, the opposition will seek to meet President Droupadi Murmu in Oct to brief her about their concerns regarding SIR and the Election Commission.The meeting was attended by Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee (TMC), Dipankar Bhattacharya (CPI-ML), Omar Abdullah (NC), Supriya Sule (NCP), Tejashwi Yadav (RJD), M A Baby (CPI-M), P Sandosh Kumar (CPI), K C Venugopal (Congress), N K Premachandran (RSP), Thol Thirumavalavan (VCK), Uddhav Thackeray (Sena UBT) and Hemant Soren (JMM).The opposition has for now paused the plan to submit a fresh removal notice against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Kharge said the opposition agrees that Kumar is working like a puppet, with PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah pulling the strings.Rahul Gandhi said he told the leaders of the bloc that they are the "collective defenders" of the Indian Constitution. "It is a personal commitment of all INDIA bloc leaders, we are going to ensure that people who have destroyed Indian democracy are punished," he said.Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee said, "We demand that Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. If he is not removed, this movement can go very far..... We have to fight this battle together." "Now it is clear, 'Vanish Kumar' is 'chor' (thief), 'daku' (dacoit)... he has stolen votes, burned, hijacked EVMs... rigged counting.... Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately," the former Bengal CM said, with Sonia sitting next to her and lauding her remarks.Rahul said there was a feeling in the room that the opposition had been successful in convincing people that elections are "stolen". "There is a new sense of resistance, particularly among young people, that what is going on in India is wrong and needs to be stopped," he added.The 19 parties included Samajwadi Party, CPI-ML, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, KC(J) and AIFB. RS MP Kapil Sibal also joined Wednesday's meet.
Article Summary: Opposition INDIA bloc announces a month-long nationwide agitation starting Oct 2. The opposition has sought immediate resignation of the chief election commissioner. The alliance will hold five major rallies in cities during Oct- Nov, including a mega rally in Delhi on Nov 1.

Article Title: Blue drum case: Meerut court convicts wife, lover for husband’s murder
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A Meerut court on Wednesday convicted Muskan Rastogi and her lover Sahil Shukla of killing her husband Saurabh Rajput in the infamous blue drum murder case.Meerut district judge Arvind Kumar Mishra ruled that Muskan , along with her boyfriend Sahil, conspired to murder her husband Saurabh Rajput and hid his body in a industrial drum using concrete and sand.The ruling came after 126 hearings and 22 witness statements.Advocate Krishan Kumar Dubey said, "The court has now held both offenders guilty of murdering Saurabh Rajput and attempting to conceal evidence related to the crime—specifically, trying to hide both the body in a blue drum and the murder weapon. Both individuals have been convicted of this offense."Muskan allegedly drugged her husband and, with Sahil's help, stabbed him to death in March, 2025. After the murder, the accused dismembered Rajput's body, placed the remains in a blue plastic drum and sealed it with cement.Muskan and Sahil subsequently fled to Himachal Pradesh and were arrested a fortnight later.
Article Summary: Meerut district judge Arvind Kumar Mishra ruled that Muskan, along with her boyfriend Sahil, conspired to murder her husband Saurabh Rajput. After the murder, the accused dismembered Rajput's body, placed the remains in a blue plastic drum and sealed it with cement.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note
Article Text:
BJP CMs Rekha Gupta, Devendra Fadnavis and Yogi Adityanath

What BJP CMs said

Rahul Gandhi’s cryptic post

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.
Article Summary: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday. The chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions” In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: Entry from 'Back Gate': School goes to cops over fake certificates
Article Text:
Sanskriti School in New Delhi's Chanakyapuri found forged disability certificates submitted for nursery admissions under CwSN (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: Sanskriti School in New Delhi's Chanakyapuri has received forged disability certificates for nursery admissions under the Children with Special Needs (CwSN) category for the 2026-27 academic session.Police sources said a senior school official wrote to Chanakyapuri police on Sept 16, seeking verification of three recommendatory letters and accompanying disability certificates submitted by parents seeking admission under CwSN quota.The documents claimed 41% hearing impairment and were purportedly issued by a Delhi govt hospital.The school told police it suspected the recommendatory letters from directorate of education, as well as the medical certificates, were not genuine and sought their verification.Chanakyapuri police subsequently conducted a preliminary inquiry. During the probe, the disability certificates annexed with the documents were verified and found to be forged.Based on the complaint and the verification, police registered a case under Sections 318(2) (cheating), 337 (forgery of record of court or of public register, etc), 340(2) (forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The exact date and time of the forgery could not be ascertained. Police will now verify the origin of the recommendatory letters, establish how the disability certificates were forged and submitted and identify those involved in the fraud. Verification of the documents purportedly issued by the hospital will also form part of the investigation. A response was sought from the school, but it had not responded till the time of publication.Cases involving forged certificates are not new to the city. In the past, multiple cases - ranging from fake marksheets to EWS certificates - have been reported. In July, police busted a shadow education network allegedly selling fake Class X and XII certificates for up to Rs 10,000 each and arrested three alleged masterminds. Police said the gang had supplied nearly 150 forged marksheets, using the expired registration of an educational institution to issue backdated certificates and make them appear genuine.
Article Summary: Sanskriti School in New Delhi's Chanakyapuri has received forged disability certificates. The certificates were for nursery admissions under the Children with Special Needs (CwSN) category. The documents claimed 41% hearing impairment and were purportedly issued by a Delhi govt hospital. The exact date and time of the forgery could not be ascertained.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Astrologer Ashok Kharat in Nashik police custody in cheating case
Article Text:
Nashik

:





Astrologer Ashok Kharat allegedly posed as a divine incarnation and promised “divine powers” and business prosperity to dupe a cloth merchant of Rs 2.6 lakh and three gold rings weighing 20gm. A city court on Wednesday remanded Kharat to police custody till Oct 2 in the cheating and Black Magic Act case registered with the Sarkarwada police on March 28.Police said Kharat convinced the merchant that gemstones provided by him would bring prosperity and divine powers. The merchant allegedly handed him three gold rings and Rs 2.6 lakh in instalments.In return, Kharat allegedly gave him fake yellow-metal rings fitted with imitation stones worth barely Rs 5,000.The alleged fraud took place in Dec 2022. The merchant, however, approached police only in March after media reports about cases of sexual assault and black magic registered against Kharat came out.Kharat has been behind bars since March 18. He faces 18 cases in Nashik and Ahilyanagar, including eight related to sexual assault. He also faces cases of cheating and one involving alleged extortion and provisions of the Black Magic Act.State govt has constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe 11 cases against Kharat. The Sarkarwada cheating case is being investigated separately.“We have received Kharat’s custody till Oct 2. Sarkarwada police will also investigate one more case against him,” investigating officer, assistant inspector Prakash Patil, said.
Article Summary: Astrologer Ashok Kharat allegedly posed as a divine incarnation and promised ‘divine powers’ and business prosperity to dupe a cloth merchant. Kharat has been behind bars since March 18. He faces 18 cases in Nashik and Ahilyanagar, including eight related to sexual assault. He also faces cases of cheating and one involving alleged extortion.

Article Title: Traffic diversions near Kasimedu signal from Oct 1
Article Text:
Traffic diversions

Chennai:





Traffic diversions will be implemented near Kasimedu signal for 15 days from Oct 1 to facilitate repairs to a damaged sewage pipeline at the junction of S N Chetty Road and Jeevarathinam Road, Chennai traffic police said.Buses and heavy vehicles proceeding towards Ennore on the outgoing side will be diverted via Jeevarathinam Road, followed by VP Koil Street and TH Road, to reach their destinations via the TH Road toll plaza junction.Two-wheelers and light motor vehicles heading towards Ennore will also be diverted via Jeevarathinam Road, VP Koil Street and TH Road. They will have to take a U-turn near Metro Rail Pillar No. 12 on TH Road and proceed via Balakrishna Street.Vehicles, including two-wheelers, light motor vehicles, buses and heavy vehicles, coming from Ennore towards Parrys on the incoming side will be diverted to the opposite carriageway at the S N Chetty Road–Power Kuppam junction, opposite the Muslim burial ground. They will then turn left and proceed via the S N Chetty Road–Kasimedu signal junction towards their destinations.Traffic police have requested motorists to cooperate with the diversions.
Article Summary: Traffic diversions will be implemented near Kasimedu signal for 15 days from Oct 1. The diversions are to facilitate repairs to a damaged sewage pipeline at the junction of S N Chetty Road and Jeevarathinam Road, Chennai traffic police said.

Article Title: Boy riding motorcycle, father booked for causing road accident in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police have registered a case against a 14-year-old boy and his father after a motorcycle ridden by the minor collided with a scooter at Gandhipuram here.According to police, the accident occurred on the 100 Feet Road around 5.35pm on Sept 22. The boy, with his father Vikram sitting on the pillion seat, was riding a motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner. The motorcycle collided with a scooter ridden by Sivakumar, 54, of Manjeshwari Colony near Kovilmedu.Due to the impact, Sivakumar fell on the road and suffered injuries on his right ankle and left elbow. He was taken to a private hospital for treatment. After treatment, Sivakumar lodged a complaint with the traffic investigation wing (east) on Tuesday.Police registered a case under sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 181(4) of the Motor Vehicles Act.Police have issued a stern warning to all parents not to allow minors without driving licences to drive vehicles.
Article Summary: Coimbatore city police have registered a case against a 14-year-old boy and his father. A motorcycle ridden by the minor collided with a scooter at Gandhipuram. The boy, with his father Vikram sitting on the pillion seat, was riding a motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.

Article Title: CM Vijay’s visit: Traffic diversions announced in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police have announced temporary traffic diversions on arterial roads in view of the visit of chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday. The CM will arrive here en route to Dharapuram, where he will be campaigning for P Sathyabama who is the TVK candidate for the Oct 6 byelection.Buses entering Coimbatore city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road. Instead, these vehicles must divert at Neelambur and take L&T Bypass via Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to enter the city. Light vehicles from the Neelambur side are also advised to go via L&T Bypass, Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to reach the city.Vehicles exiting the city via the Avinashi Road must make a U-turn at Lakshmi Mills Junction and proceed via Puliyakulam, Ramanathapuram and Singanallur to reach L&T Bypass.Light motor vehicles exiting via the Avinashi Road and the V K Road should take a diversion through the Masakalipalayam Road to reach Singanallur. Vehicles arriving via Avinashi Road / Hope College Junction must make a U-turn at Tidel Park Junction and proceed via the Kamarajar Road to Singanallur.Heavy vehicles heading towards the Avinashi Road from Kalapatti Junction must divert at Kalapatti Junction and proceed via Thennampalayam.Heavy vehicles approaching the Avinashi Road from the Goldwins Road should turn right at the Housing Unit Road / Maruti Bakery Junction and proceed via the Veeriyampalayam Road to reach Kalapatti Junction.Passengers are advised to reach the airport at least 30 minutes prior to their scheduled travel time. Parking for call taxis and private vehicles on the airport premises will not be permitted.Entry of trucks into the city is prohibited between 7am and 9pm on Wednesday.Trucks travelling from Walayar towards Salem on the Kochi - Salem National Highway are advised to take the alternative route via Palathurai Junction and Karpagam College Junction towards Othakkalmandapam, Chettipalayam, Pappampatti, Selakarichal and Karadivavi. Trucks going towards Walayar are advised to travel to Sulur via Chinthamanipudur and Pappampatti. Trucks travelling from Annur towards Avinashi and Karumathampatti are prohibited from passing through Somanur.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay will arrive in Coimbatore on Wednesday. Buses entering city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road.

Article Title: HC directs DVAC to probe complaint of money collection for advocate posts
Article Text: Madras high court has directed officials of Nagercoil directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) to conduct an inquiry into a complaint alleging that an advocate with political affiliation collected huge sums of money from practising advocates in Kanyakumari district by assuring govt advocate posts.
Article Summary: Madras high court has directed officials of Nagercoil directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) to conduct an inquiry into a complaint. The complaint alleges that an advocate with political affiliation collected huge sums of money from practising advocates in Kanyakumari district.

Article Title: Woman cop dies after chasing assault suspect in Paramakudi
Article Text:
head constable kannagi (file picture)

Ramanathapuram

:





A woman head constable collapsed and died while chasing a 25-year-old man who allegedly assaulted another person in the emergency ward of the Paramakudi govt hospital on Monday. Police arrested the man on Tuesday in connection with the incident.Police said M Kannagi, a woman head constable, was on duty at the police assistance centre in the emergency ward of the hospital around 8pm on Monday when she witnessed a man slap another person.Kannagi immediately attempted to apprehend the alleged assailant. The man allegedly pushed her aside and tried to flee. Undeterred, Kannagi chased him for about 50m, but he managed to escape from the hospital premises.Police said Kannagi subsequently returned to the emergency ward and went to the dressing room, where she suddenly fainted. Nurses rushed her to doctors, who administered CPR and made efforts to revive her. However, she died despite treatment.Paramakudi Town police registered a case and launched a search for the man who had fled the hospital.Following an investigation, police arrested the suspect, identified as Karuvayan alias Karuppuraja, of Kumarakurichi in Sivaganga district, on Tuesday morning.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay offered his condolences and announced Rs30 lakh for the family of the bereaved.
Article Summary: M Kannagi, a woman head constable, was on duty at the police assistance centre in the emergency ward of the Paramakudi govt hospital on Monday. She witnessed a man slap another person and attempted to apprehend the alleged assailant. The man allegedly pushed her aside and tried to flee. Police arrested the man on Tuesday in connection with the incident.

Article Title: Fresh summons to Anto Augustine over ‘CM marriage’ remarks
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Kalamassery Police has sent a fresh summons to Reporter TV managing director Anto Augustine over alleged defamatory remarks against CM V D Satheesan.Augustine has been directed to appear before investigators at 10am on Thursday. The second notice was issued after he missed a scheduled questioning session on Monday, citing personal inconvenience. Meanwhile, Augustine has approached the high court to quash the FIR.The standard procedure involves issuing three notices before informing the court if a suspect repeatedly fails to appear, police said.The case is based on a complaint by Congress spokesperson Raju P Nair, who alleged a conspiracy behind Augustine’s recent public statements. Augustine had claimed that two individuals approached his news channel with unverified reports regarding Satheesan’s alleged second marriage, but the channel chose not to broadcast the story after failing to verify the claims.
Article Summary: Anto Augustine has been directed to appear before investigators at 10am on Thursday. The second notice was issued after he missed a scheduled questioning session on Monday, citing personal inconvenience. Augustine has approached the high court to quash the FIR. The case is based on a complaint by Congress spokesperson Raju P Nair.
